gen-fs-expose-gf-vend-sans: Striking and tightly packed, Expose barely pauses between lowercase and caps. Vend Sans draws a ruler-straight line of constant width with a tall x-height, with no brush-style pressure swell anywhere.
gen-fs-kohinoor-zerone-gf-orbit: Kohinoor Zerone draws its round letters like bent wire, precise and distinctly contemporary. Orbit loosens the mood with curves that stop short of closing, each character floating apart in a rope-like stroke.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-amiko: Technical to the bone, Nippo lifts its small letters almost to capital height, strokes cut like wire. Amiko brings terminals that point outward like tongs, a sans-serif partner whose own tall lowercase keeps pace with the heading.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-anek-bangla: Lowercase that stands almost as tall as the capitals gives Nippo its wire-cut, technical look. But Anek Bangla is the approachable one, with wide s curves barely curled in and a short stretch from midline to ascender.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-anek-gurmukhi: Small letters nearly capital-sized make Nippo look cut from wire. The heading holds every stroke hairline-free and technical, while Anek Gurmukhi brings generous round curves and big open counters.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-anek-kannada: Nippo's small letters rise nearly to capital height, drawn like wire with no contrast from stem to terminal. Anek Kannada echoes that height with a woodblock-high x-height, its terminals stopping well away from the stem.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-anek-odia: Nippo glows like neon tubing, its small letters nearly as tall as its capitals. Anek Odia leaves its rounds unsealed like an unlatched hook and keeps capitals only slightly above lowercase, so the two rhyme in height.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-arimo: Arimo brings a tall mean line and spacious gaps in its rounded letters, a steady partner for Nippo. And down a full page of it, the text would read smoothly, with no heavy-to-hairline swings to snag the eye.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-armata: Small letters nearly capital-sized give Nippo its wire-cut look, with no swing in stroke weight. And Armata, with spacious gaps between characters and lowercase filling most of the letter height, would read steadily across a full column.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-athiti: Contemporary and technical, Nippo lifts small letters almost to capital height, each stroke cut like wire. But Athiti is the approachable one, with a see-through gap in each s and a high mean line.
